title: fix(spec): the script.config.template tombstone points at the notify node's own template key
body:
Closes #24965

Clause-②: no (prose only: no shape, key, default or accepted value moves)

## What changed

The `script.config.template` tombstone in `packages/spec/src/automation/schemaless-node-config.zod.ts` told authors that "stored templates live in the messaging service (`sys_notification_template`), not on the node". That text predates the `notify` node's own `template` key. This is the spec-lane half of execution card ② of ruling D on #24770 (decision `6290342354`, recorded by triage in `6293376907`). The services half is #24924.

The prescription now reads:

> Delete the key. For templated content use a `notify` node and name an email template (`email_template`) in its own `template` key, with `templateData` filling its placeholders: the email and in-app inbox channels render that template in each recipient's locale. Otherwise the node carries inline `title`/`message`. The messaging service's `sys_notification_template` rows are read only by the `email` and `sms` channels, `email` only when the node names no template.

The `retiredKey()` call, the key's rejection and every other tombstone are unchanged. The generated reference `content/docs/references/automation/schemaless-node-config.mdx` was regenerated with `gen:docs` and carries the same text. No test pins the old wording (`git grep "stored templates live"` on the base finds only the source and the generated page).

## Claims verified against the runtime (origin/main `2b1382a5b3`)

| Claim in the new text | Evidence |
|:--|:--|
| `notify` has its own `template` key naming an `email_template`, and `templateData` fills its placeholders | `packages/spec/src/automation/io-node-config.zod.ts:585` (`template`, described as an `email_template` item's `name`), `:593` (`templateData`); `email_template` is a metadata type at `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts:162` |
| The executor forwards the template reference, not inline content, when one is named | `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-node.ts:465` reads `cfg.template`; `:614-616` puts `{ template, templateData }` in the payload, else `{ title, body }` |
| The email channel renders the named template per recipient locale and does not read `sys_notification_template` then | `packages/services/service-messaging/src/email-channel.ts:330-333` takes `payload.template`, `:345` calls `email.sendTemplate`, and that branch returns before `:378`, the only `store.load(…, 'email', …)` |
| The inbox channel renders the named template per recipient locale | `packages/services/service-messaging/src/inbox-channel.ts:163-166` takes `payload.template`, `:182` resolves the recipient locale, `:188` calls `email.renderTemplate` |
| The inbox never reads `sys_notification_template` | `packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service-plugin.ts:285` builds the inbox channel with no `store`; only the email (`:398`) and sms (`:417`) channels get `templateStore` |
| `sms` reads `sys_notification_template` whether or not a template is named | `packages/services/service-messaging/src/sms-channel.ts:285` calls `store.load(topic, 'sms', …)` unconditionally; the file reads no `payload.template` |
| Without a template, the node carries inline `title`/`message` | `notify-node.ts:508` (title required when no template), `io-node-config.zod.ts:559`/`:562` |

The services side states the same reader set: `packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/notification-template.object.ts:6-27` (`TEMPLATE_CHANNELS = ['email', 'sms']`).

**One deviation from the dispatch wording.** The dispatch said a named template "is used on every channel". The runtime shows otherwise for `sms`: it has no template path and reads `sys_notification_template` (falling back to the topic) even when the node names an email template. So the text names email and inbox as the channels that render the named template. It says `sys_notification_template` is read by `email` only when no template is named, and it does not say the same of `sms`.
